items.title: 10.18 Variation of E value with ion concentration

source_refs.note: Topic 10.18 with Table 10.1, printed page 234. The table's up/down arrows are read as above/below 1.00 mol dm-3.

blocks.text: The position of an equilibrium is affected by changes in concentration, temperature and pressure, so changing the concentration or temperature of a half-cell changes its electrode potential; under non-standard conditions the symbol E is used. For the metal/metal ion equilibrium Zn2+(aq) + 2e- giving Zn(s), E standard = -0.76 V: if [Zn2+] is greater than 1.00 mol dm-3 the value of E becomes less negative (more positive), say -0.61 V; if [Zn2+] is less than 1.00 mol dm-3, E becomes more negative (less positive), say -0.80 V. Le Chatelier's principle applies to redox equilibria: increasing the concentration of the species on the left shifts the equilibrium to the right, so E becomes more positive (less negative).

If two different ions are present in the half-cell both must be considered, as for Fe3+ + e- giving Fe2+, E standard = +0.77 V with both ions at 1.00 mol dm-3. Table 10.1 shows the effect: raising [Fe3+] above 1.00 or lowering [Fe2+] below 1.00 makes E more positive (+0.85 V); lowering [Fe3+] or raising [Fe2+] makes it less positive (+0.70 V).

blocks.caption: Variation of potential with ion concentration (Table 10.1; arrows read as above or below 1.00 mol dm-3)

blocks.prompt: What is the effect of a change in ion concentration on the electrode potential of a half-reaction (Quick Check 10.9b)?
blocks.explanation: Raising the concentration of the oxidised species on the left pushes the reduction equilibrium to the right and makes E more positive; raising the reduced species on the right, or lowering the left-hand ion, pushes it left and makes E more negative. Only under the standard 1.00 mol dm-3 conditions does E equal E standard.

items: Non-standard E: more Zn2+ makes E less negative (-0.61 V), less Zn2+ more negative (-0.80 V); Le Chatelier: more of the left-hand species shifts right, E more positive; Fe3+/Fe2+ (+0.77 V) goes to +0.85 or +0.70 V as the ratio changes.
